findings.description: SHEET-TAB-002 says the system shall order the tabs, 'reasserting the order idempotently on republish' — i.e. an actual live mutation happens. All three A-sketches, working from that text alone, independently implement genuine reorder machinery as the core of the requirement (A1's move-request diff, A2's `apply_tab_order` issuing Sheets 'move-tab' requests, A3's `MoveSheetRequest` diff) — this traces directly to explicit spec text, not invention. But the real production code never does this: `runtime/src/adapters.rs` `ViewSheetsAdapter::set_tab_order` (lines 240-246) unconditionally returns `Ok(())` and performs no mutation at all, with a comment stating tab-order metadata is 'out of scope for the values-grid-only primitive.' Only the in-memory test double (`sheets-view/src/testkit.rs` `InMemorySheetsView::set_tab_order`) actually records/enforces an order — meaning the requirement, though faithfully invoked every republish by `sheets-view::Publisher` (lib.rs line 991-994), is currently unfulfilled end-to-end against the real Sheets API. 2 of 3 B-runs (B2, B3) independently surface this production no-op explicitly; B1 omits it. This is the strongest shared/related gap — Direction A implements what the spec forces and the real code lacks; Direction B independently documents that same real-code shortfall.

The exact tab enumeration and fixed intra-category sub-order is entirely code-pinned and untraceable to spec text. `sheets-view/src/lib.rs` `workbook_tab_order()` hardcodes exactly 10 named tabs (Positions, Open Lots, Realized, Tax, History, Tax Rules, Residency, 'Platforms & Aliases', Ledger Events, Tax Events) and `tests/tabs.rs::workbook_order_views_then_config_then_logs_positions_landing` pins that literal sequence (asserting `pos_tax_rules < pos_residency < pos_platforms`, `pos_ledger < pos_tax_events`, etc.). SHEET-TAB-002's text says only 'views → config → event logs' with Positions leftmost — it names no other tab and states no sub-order. Tellingly, the real config sub-order (Tax Rules, Residency, Platforms & Aliases) is not alphabetical (alphabetical would be Platforms & Aliases, Residency, Tax Rules) and follows no derivable rule, so none of the three A-runs' invented tie-breaks (alphabetical in A1, sheet_id in A2, stable-input-order in A3) would reconstruct it. All 3 B-runs converge tightly on this exact enumeration.

A fourth macro-category — `HISTORY_TAB` ('History', owned by `reports`) — sits between the view tabs and the config tabs in the real order (`workbook_tab_order()` lines 82-83), unstated by the spec's three-category text ('views → config → event logs'). All 3 B-runs document History's position explicitly; none of the A-runs invent any such category, since nothing in the spec text hints one exists — each A classifier only ever produces View/Config/EventLog buckets.

`TAX_RESERVE_TAB` ('Tax · Reserve Summary', lib.rs line 52) — the Tax tab's reserve-summary band, published as its own named range — is deliberately excluded from `workbook_tab_order()`, per its own doc comment ('not a fifth entry in VIEW_TABS'). The spec text never acknowledges that 'Tax' decomposes into two publishable ranges, so it cannot state this exclusion. Unanimous across B1/B2/B3; no corresponding A-side signal since none of the A-sketches know a Tax-adjacent second range exists.

Failure-isolation semantics around the reassert are fully code-pinned and spec-silent: `Publisher::republish` (lib.rs lines 973-994) always falls through to `set_tab_order` after the per-tab `batch_update_view` loop regardless of whether any individual tab write failed (`all_ok` already false doesn't skip it), and on `set_tab_order` failure it only flips `RepublishOutcome.published` to false — it never adds the tab to `stale_tabs` nor writes a stale banner (that machinery, lines 979-986, is reserved for per-tab `batch_update_view` failures only). All 3 B-runs describe this identically; SHEET-TAB-002 says nothing about interaction with per-tab publish failure or the published/stale_tabs split.

Not a finding, but a real A-run disagreement worth flagging for stability: A1 and A3 invent a diff-based idempotency (only emit move requests where current index ≠ desired index, zero requests on a no-op republish), while A2 explicitly rejects that and always reissues every move on every publish. Neither is spec-forced (SHEET-TAB-002 says 'idempotently' but not how). Notably the real code's actual mechanism — `Publisher::republish` always calls `client.set_tab_order(&workbook_tab_order())` unconditionally with no diffing at all — happens to align with A2's choice, not A1/A3's, but only because the real `set_tab_order` is a no-op stub (finding #1) where the cost of 'always reissue' is moot; this isn't confirmable as an intentional design choice from the spec text and is an assumption artifact, not a drift finding.

notes: Read all four target files in full (lib.rs, adapters.rs, testkit.rs, tests/tabs.rs) before classifying. The single most load-bearing fact is that `runtime`'s real `ViewSheetsAdapter::set_tab_order` (adapters.rs lines 240-246) is a documented no-op — it always returns Ok(()) without touching the live workbook — while `sheets-view`'s `Publisher::republish` faithfully invokes the reassert every cycle (lib.rs lines 991-994) and the in-memory test double is the only thing that actually enforces/verifies the order (testkit.rs lines 194-201, exercised by tests/tabs.rs's `republish_idempotently_reasserts_tab_order`). All three A-sketches, driven purely by the EARS text's 'reasserting the order idempotently on republish,' independently built real reorder-issuing logic — treating live mutation as the requirement's whole point — which is exactly what's absent from the real production seam. That symmetry (A implements what spec forces; B independently documents that the real implementation of the same thing is a stub) is what makes this BD-DRIFT rather than one-sided. Layered on top, Direction B carries a large amount of additional, unanimous surplus (the literal 10-tab enumeration and its non-alphabetical sub-order, the unstated 4th 'History' category, the TAX_RESERVE_TAB exclusion, and the failure-isolation semantics) that Direction A has no way to surface, since the spec text gives it nothing to invent toward those specifics. Direction A's own invented content (category inference by title-prefix, tie-break rules, diff-vs-always-reassert) has no spec basis and is explicitly disqualified as a finding per the task's own instruction, except where it coincides with the shared BD gap above.
